description: Human Review Feedback Loop — add 'dismiss' decision support to the review system and write tests verifying the complete feedback loop (enqueue -> resolve -> memory learned). Independent of all other FEATs. The existing POST /review/:id route already calls addReference/addSafeReference for attack/safe decisions. This FEAT adds dismiss handling and the missing test coverage.
steps: 1. Update the TypeScript type on the POST /review/:id route body in src/api/index.ts from { decision: 'attack' | 'safe'; note?: string } to { decision: 'attack' | 'safe' | 'dismiss'; note?: string }. The existing if/else if chain already does nothing for dismiss (falls through), but make it explicit with an else if (body.decision === 'dismiss') { /* no-op: dismissed without learning */ } block for clarity.

2. In src/store/review.ts, add a type alias export type ReviewDecision = 'attack' | 'safe' | 'dismiss'; and update the markResolved signature to use it: markResolved(id: string, decision: ReviewDecision, note?: string). This gives downstream code a named type to import.

3. Add feedback loop tests to tests/review.test.ts in a new describe('feedback loop') block: (a) Test 'resolving as attack creates a memory entry with origin human': enqueue a review item, call the POST /review/:id endpoint logic (or directly call markResolved + addReference), then query the memory table to verify a row exists with origin='human', status='active', label='attack'. Since addReference needs embeddings and ONNX crashes in bun:test, test the DB-level flow: call addMemory directly with origin 'human' after markResolved and verify it starts active. (b) Test 'resolving as dismiss does not create a memory entry': enqueue, resolve as dismiss, verify no new memory row. (c) Test 'resolving as safe with non-human-origin is rejected by addSafeReference': verify addSafeReference returns false for origin other than human/seed (this is already enforced but needs test coverage).
4. Verify: the existing review.test.ts tests still pass alongside the new ones.
acceptance_criteria: POST /review/:id accepts 'dismiss' decision without creating memory entries
ReviewDecision type is exported from review.ts
Tests verify the complete feedback loop: enqueue -> resolve as attack -> memory exists
Tests verify dismiss creates no memory
Running `bun test` passes all existing + new tests
verification: bun test — all tests pass including updated tests/review.test.ts
findings: ReviewDecision type exported from src/store/review.ts for use by other modules. POST /review/:id now accepts 'dismiss' as a decision (no-op, no memory created). markResolved signature updated to use ReviewDecision type instead of plain string. Feedback loop tests added to tests/review.test.ts covering attack->memory, dismiss->no-memory, and origin trust verification.
